title: PartCollection::add_part() documented footgun: inferred total causes is_complete() false positive
description: PartCollection in uuencoding-multi/src/collection.rs infers total_parts from the first part added if not set externally. A caller that adds exactly one part (part 1 of N, where N > 1) will find is_complete() returning true because the inferred total equals the count of inserted parts. The doc comment acknowledges this but every caller must know to set the total explicitly before adding parts — the type system provides no guard against the wrong order of operations. What goes wrong: a caller that iterates messages in arrival order, adds part 1 first, and immediately checks is_complete() will incorrectly believe the file is ready and call reassemble(), which will silently produce a truncated output (or panic, depending on implementation). The fix is either: (a) remove inference — require total_parts at construction time so is_complete() is always meaningful; or (b) return a distinct state from is_complete() that communicates 'total is inferred, not confirmed'. File: uuencoding-multi/src/collection.rs.
close_reason: Already documented with a warning in the PartCollection::add_part() doc comment. The false-positive is_complete() behavior is a documented tradeoff for the Usenet use case where total is commonly inferred from the subject line.
